Subject: Checkout slowdowns during peak personalization window

Diego —

We started seeing a spike in checkout latency yesterday evening that lines up with your personalization calls (personalize-v2). The symptom: a small percentage (~3-5%) of requests are taking 10–25s and failing the client-side timeout. That’s translating to cart abandonment on several SKUs.

We narrowed it to the personalization path (calls to your hosted endpoint) — attached are a sample of traces and a dashboard screenshot. We’re in the middle of a promotion and this is causing visible revenue impact. Can you own a priority triage? We need: 1) a short explanation of root cause, 2) immediate mitigations you can push today, and 3) a timeline for a complete fix.

Attached: request_traces_20280906.log (logs.zip), dashboard_screenshot.png

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-09-06T18:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Checkout slowdowns during peak personalization window

Quick triage notes — reproduced from traces you sent: a few characteristics stand out:
- Tail-only phenomenon: 97th–99.9th percentile token latencies spike during rolling 10–15 minute windows that align with Brightleaf’s promo bursts.
- Queueing evidence: traces show sustained inflight request backlog at the personalization model pool; individual requests sit queued for 6–12s before getting GPU attention.
- Concurrency cap hits: per-customer concurrency for Brightleaf hit the configured soft cap intermittently; autoscaling did not immediately provision due to fragmentation on the node pool.
- Error surface: when queueing hit threshold we observed a small bump in 429/503s (retry exhaustion) and client timeouts.

Preliminary root cause hypothesis: workload spike + request fanout pattern (Brightleaf sends a burst of independent personalization calls per checkout) caused temporary queue saturation and delayed KV cache warmup for some models.

Immediate suggestions (can apply in minutes):
1) Temporary routing to a slightly smaller-but-faster quantized model (reduces per-token GPU work) for the promo window.
2) Short-term concurrency cap increase for Brightleaf to allow higher in-flight requests.
3) Enable aggressive prefix caching for personalization keys that are high-frequency during the promo.

I’ll prepare traces with request IDs mapped to queue timestamps and upload analysis (tail-analysis-v1.pdf).

— Karthik
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@brightleaf.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@brightleaf.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-06T19:01:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed immediate mitigations — Brightleaf personalization

Hi Sanjay / Priya —

Thanks for the quick samples. Karthik has found clear queueing and soft concurrency cap behavior. We can implement the following mitigations within 30–45 minutes (no code changes required):

1) Route Brightleaf personalize-v2 traffic to quantized-128 variant for the next 6 hours (reduces median token time by ~18% in our benchmarks).
2) Temporarily increase Brightleaf’s per-customer concurrency soft cap from 40 -> 60 during peak hours for the next 24 hours.
3) Turn on prefix caching for the top 200 personalization keys to reduce duplicated decoder work (cache TTL 15m).

Risks & notes: the concurrency bump will increase short-term cost; the quantized variant has slightly different token calibration — we’ll watch output quality closely for regressions and can revert if you see issues.

If you approve, Ben will apply the config change and monitor. We’ll provide hourly status updates and a short RCA within 48 hours.

Attachments: tail-analysis-v1.pdf

Monica Patel
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference

Sanjay

Subject: Exec readout and customer next steps — Brightleaf incident

Folks — looping Laura and Ben for exec visibility. Summary for leadership:

- Impact: Brightleaf experienced ~3–5% of personalization requests that entered long-tail queueing (10–25s) during promo bursts; led to ~4.1% drop in conversion over the promo window.
- Root cause (prelim): request burst pattern + per-customer concurrency soft cap + node fragmentation prevented autoscaling from immediately absorbing the load; KV cache warmup contributed to per-request decoding overhead.
- Steps taken (already applied): routing to quantized-128 model, concurrency soft cap increased 40->60, aggressive prefix caching enabled. Customer-facing comms drafted; Ben to send.
- Next actions: 1) complete RCA with per-request timeline (Karthik, 48h), 2) evaluate long-term options: predictive scaling for promo windows, token pre-warming, and a reserved capacity offer for Brightleaf (Monica/Ben, 72h), 3) propose a goodwill credit (finance + revenue ops) — Ben, please advise amount.

Meeting: I’ve scheduled a 30m sync with Brightleaf for 2028-09-07 11:00 PST (invite sent). Laura — can you join to cover exec comms?

Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Accounts Lead, Redwood Inference
